recent_items.title: Savoy Declaration Ch.3 Sec.1
recent_items.description: Chapter 3: Of God's Eternal Decree Section 1 God from all eternity did, by the most wise and holy counsel of his own will, freely and unchangeably ordain whatsoever comes to pass; yet so as thereby neither is God the author of sin, nor is violence offered to the will of the creatures, nor is the liberty or contingency of second causes taken away, but rather established.

recent_items.title: Thirty-nine Articles of Religion Art.4
recent_items.description: Article 4: Of the Resurrection of Christ. Christ did truly rise again from death, and took again his body, with flesh, bones, and all things appertaining to the perfection of Man's nature; wherewith he ascended into Heaven, and there sitteth, until he return to judge all Men at the last day.

recent_items.title: Westminster Shorter Catechism Q10
recent_items.description: Q10. How did God create man? A. God created man male and female, after his own image, in knowledge, righteousness, and holiness, with dominion over the creatures.

recent_items.title: Second Helvetic Confession Ch.5 Sec.5
recent_items.description: Chapter 5: Of The Adoration, Worship and Invocation of God Through The Only Mediator Jesus Christ Section 5 RELICS OF THE SAINTS Much less do we believe that the relics of the saints are to be adored and reverenced. Those ancient saints seemed to have sufficiently honored their dead when they decently committed their remains to the earth after the spirit had ascended on high. And they thought that the most noble relics of their ancestors were their virtues, their doctrine, and their faith. Moreover, as they commend these "relics" when praising the dead, so they strive to copy them during their life on earth.

recent_items.title: Martin Luther's 95 theses Thesis 9
recent_items.description: Thesis 9 Therefore the Holy Spirit through the pope is kind to us insofar as the pope in his decrees always makes exception of the article of death and of necessity.

recent_items.title: Heidelberg Catechism Q12
recent_items.description:
Q12. Since, according to God's righteous judgment we deserve temporal and eternal punishment, how can we escape this punishment and be again received into favour? A. God demands that His justice be satisfied. Therefore full payment must be made either by ourselves or by another.
Scripture References: [1] Exod.20.5, Exod.23.7, Rom.2.1-Rom.2.11 [2] Isa.53.11, Rom.8.3-Rom.8.4

recent_items.title: Westminster Larger Catechism Q18
recent_items.description:
Q18. What are God's works of providence? A. God's works of providence are his most holy, wise, and powerful preserving and governing all his creatures; ordering them, and all their actions, to his own glory.
Scripture References: [1] Ps.145.17 [2] Ps.104.24, Isa.28.29 [3] Heb.1.8 [4] Ps.103.19 [5] Matt.10.29-Matt.10.31, Gen.45.7 [6] Rom.11.36, Isa.43.14

recent_items.title: Westminster Confession of Faith Ch.3 Sec.3
recent_items.description:
Chapter 3: Of God's Eternal Decree Section 3 By the decree of God, for the manifestation of his glory, some men and angels[1] are predestinated unto everlasting life, and others fore-ordained to everlasting death.[2]
Scripture References: [1] Matt.25.41, 1Tim.5.21 [2] Prov.16.4, Rom.9.22-Rom.9.23, Eph.1.5-Eph.1.6

recent_items.title: London Baptist Confession of 1689 Ch.3 Sec.2
recent_items.description: Chapter 3: Of God's Decree Section 2 Although God knoweth whatsoever may, or can come to passe upon all supposed conditions; yet hath he not Decreed anything, because he foresaw it as future, or as that which would come to pass upon such conditions.
